On Mon, Jul 20, 2026 at 10:18 PM Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com> wrote:
> Team — forwarding NextWave report. Paging infra/serving leads.

Initial findings from the affected serving pool:
- We see a correlated increase in KV cache eviction rate starting 21:40 PT. That aligns with elevated per-request latency and a growing KV miss amplification.
- Batching windows for the NextWave model variant were automatically widened by the autoscaler to try to improve throughput; that increased head-of-line wait time for short requests.
- No OOMs or GPU saturation reported; CPU on the router nodes briefly hit 85% on one host.

Immediate mitigation applied (21:55 PT):
1) Reverted batching window to baseline for the NextWave routing policy.
2) Forced a redis shard failover for one proxy where eviction was highest.
3) Spun up two extra dedicated instances in the us-west pool to buffer traffic.

I've attached the service logs for the 21:30–22:30 window (svc_error_logs_20260720.zip). Monitoring shows error rate trending down but p95 still elevated (~650ms) — need 30–45m to validate full recovery under production load.

Marcus Lin
Director, Serving Runtime
